question: Which of the following best describes a Level III ICU?

answers.text: A ward area with enhanced nursing observation but no mechanical ventilation capability

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This describes a High-Dependency Unit (HDU) or Level I ICU, not a Level III.

answers.text: A unit capable of full multi-organ support, 24-hour intensivist cover, and on-site subspecialty services

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Level III (tertiary) ICUs provide full multi-organ support with continuous intensivist presence and access to all subspecialties.

answers.text: A unit that provides single-organ ventilatory support with daytime consultant cover only

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Single-organ support with daytime-only cover is characteristic of a Level II ICU.

answers.text: A post-operative recovery bay with monitoring but no ventilator beds

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A post-anaesthesia care unit (PACU) handles short-term recovery; it is not classified as a Level III ICU.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review ICU classification: Level I = high-dependency/monitoring only; Level II = single-organ support with limited specialist cover; Level III = full multi-organ support with 24/7 intensivist and subspecialty access.
Well done. Level III ICUs are tertiary referral centres with the highest intensity of monitoring, organ support, and specialist cover.
